trust_decision.summary: Which trailer field names may be accepted and merged into request (or response) headers is decided by a deny-list bitmask in http_request_trailer_check(); the test used the raw enum id instead of light_bshift(id), so forbidden names such as Content-Length, Host or Authorization were not reliably rejected before the merge.

landing_point.why: The summary says trailers are merged into headers after HTTP request parsing; h1_chunked_trailers() is the HTTP/1.1 merge loop (src/h1.c:639-651) and calls the check at src/h1.c:615. The bug is one hop away in src/request.c.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP/1.1 chunked request body trailers (h1_chunked -> h1_chunked_trailers -> http_request_trailers_check, src/h1.c:615); HTTP/2 HEADERS-frame trailers (http_request_parse_single_trailer, src/request.c:555); backend chunked response trailers (http_chunk_decode_append_trailers, src/http_chunk.c:336)
fix_sites.module_kind: core request parser / shared validation helper

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All three routes (H1 request, H2 request, backend response trailers) call the one fixed function, so a single change covers them: src/h1.c:615, src/request.c:555, src/http_chunk.c:336.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No route is left open after the one-line fix. The only arguable areas are names missing from the deny list (e.g. Cookie, X-Forwarded-For, Proxy-Authorization), and a solver can say those are list policy, not the advisory bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Arbitrary non-forbidden trailers that are declared in the Trailer header must still be merged into request headers and reach the backend (CGI env HTTP_TEST_TRAILER echo). A fix that drops or rejects all trailers breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: HTTP/1.1 chunked request trailer with a known-enum forbidden name (e.g. Content-Length)
HTTP/2 HEADERS (END_STREAM) trailer with a known-enum forbidden name
backend chunked response trailer with a known-enum forbidden name (dropped rather than 400)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The response-side merge loop re-parses gw_dechunk->b and inserts every field into response headers. It relies on validation done earlier in src/http_chunk.c:336, so a planted path that fills gw_dechunk->b without that check (or a separate response-only deny list) would be realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comments at src/response.c:593 and :598 already say '(checked in http_request_trailers_check())', so a maintainer could plausibly split request and response policy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The HTTP/2 trailer path builds its own tpctx per field (hlen reset to 0 at src/request.c:549) and could plausibly carry its own inline deny check that drifts from the H1 one.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment at src/request.c:530 calls it the 'HTTP/2 version of src/h1.c:h1_chunked_trailers()', i.e. it is a parallel implementation.

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / header smuggling via trailer-to-header merge (CWE-444); a broken bitmask deny-list check

O10_build.toolchain: meson/ninja, autotools or cmake with a C compiler; Perl for tests/*.t
O10_build.project_tests: tests/request.t (Perl LightyTest harness, starts a local lighttpd and runs cgi.pl; trailer cases at tests/request.t:262-297); src/t/test_request.c has no trailer unit tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding name check in the h1.c merge loop (src/h1.c:639-651), which leaves the broken bitmask, the H2 path and the response path unfixed. Or stop merging trailers entirely, which breaks the legitimate trailer echo.

out_of_scope_notes: The deny list omits some security-relevant names that end up merged into backend-visible headers (e.g. Cookie, X-Forwarded-For, Proxy-Authorization, Content-Location); this is policy breadth, not the advisory's bitmask bug.

In the HTTP/2 trailer path, tpctx.hlen restarts at 0 for each field (src/request.c:549), so the cumulative oversized-trailers check at src/request.c:1458-1462 is per field there; resource limit, not pursued.
